summary: Syed Ali Bilgrami (1853–1911) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Lucknow, Patna College, IIT Roorkee, the Royal School of Mines, and London, he worked for the Government of Hyderabad (~1879–1901) and was Reader in Marathi at Cambridge (1901).

Syed Ameer Ali (1849–1928) was a historian and religious studies scholar. He studied at Aliah University and the University of Calcutta (~1867–1869), later holding a post at the University of Calcutta from circa 1877 to 1881.

Syed Hasan Askari (1901–1990) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College (~1918–1922), and Patna University (~1922–1924), and served as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.
Syed Nawab Ali (1878–1958) was a scholar in history and archaeology. In 1932, he was attested as Professor of Persian at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and as Principal of Bahauddin College.
Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1980) and under Marie-Claude Porcher, and held a post at Aix-Marseille University.

Sylvain Lévi (1863–1935) was a French scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the EPHE (~1886–1935), the Collège de France (1894–1935), and served as president of the Maison Franco-Japonaise (1926–1928).
Søren Sørensen (1848–1902) was an Indologist. He held posts at Herlufsholm School (1876–1878) and at the University of Copenhagen (~1887–1902).
Sāmaṇera Bodhesako (1939–1988) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Path Press and served as an editor at the Buddhist Publication Society.
Sīlaratano is a monastic scholar who studied under Narada Maha Thera, Ajahn Maha Bua, and Nyanaponika Thera.

Sōen Shaku (1860–1919) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Keio University and under multiple teachers, including Kosen Imakita. He served as Zen master at Engaku-ji (1892) and president of Hanazono University (1914–1917).
Sōkatsu Shaku (1870–1954) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Kosen Imakita and Sōen Shaku. He founded the Ryōbōkai (1901), Ryobokai (1906), and the Ningen Zen Kyodan.

Sōkō Morinaga (1925–1995) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Toyama High School and Daitoku-ji under Sesso Oda and Zuigan Goto, later serving as head of Hanazono University (1986–1994) and abbot of Daiju-in (~1963–1995).

T. Chandrasekharan was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He was attested in 1951 as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at Madras Sanskrit College, succeeding T. R. Chintamani.

T. Griffith Foulk is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez, later teaching there (~1987–1995) and serving as Riggs Professor of Religion at Sarah Lawrence College.
T. K. V. Desikachar (1938–2016) was an Indology and religious studies figure. He studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from circa 1961 to 1989 and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

T. N. Ramachandran (1901–1973) was an archaeologist and Indologist. He served as archaeologist at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1928–1934) and curator of archaeology at the National Museum, New Delhi.
T. R. Chintamani was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras from circa 1930 to 1945.

T. R. V. Murti (1902–1986) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. Supervised by Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, he earned a D.Litt. from Banaras Hindu University, later holding professorships at Banaras Hindu University (~1953–1967) and McMaster University (~1970–1975).
T. S. Srinivasa Sastri was an Indology and philosophy scholar who served at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where he was attested as a professor between 1984 and 1992.

T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as Professor of Advaita Vedānta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).
